summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted with a severe posterior headache, neck stiffness, and low-grade fever. Initial evaluation included a normal head CT and lumbar puncture showing no signs of infection. She had new subcutaneous nodules on her left leg, concerning for septic emboli, prompting dermatology consultation and biopsy, which showed only extravasated red blood cells. Blood cultures were negative, and echocardiogram showed no new vegetation, though a calcified mitral valve area could not be fully ruled out. Liver enzymes were acutely elevated but improved rapidly, with hepatology attributing this to a likely passed biliary stone. The fever resolved without a definitive source, and the headache subsided after admission. She was treated with IV antibiotics initially but was transitioned to oral care as her condition stabilized. She was discharged home afebrile with instructions to follow up on pending labs, dental care, and outpatient appointments.
